text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Several state-owned power firms want to become limited companies as a first step towards privatization. Last week power companies in three of Norway's largest cities decided to register as limited companies.

- Oil companies and the industry in general are having trouble reaching the goals set by the NORSOK programme. The programme aims to improve the Norwegian oil industry's ability to compete with foreign oil industris. All the current development projects are either overdue or more expensive than earlier believed.

- Buro Scandinavia, which markets holidays to Norway in Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg, says foreign tourists in northern Norway are treated like cattle. Buro Scandinavia's Martin de Ruiter says standards of food and the hotel accommodation are poor, while the attitudes towards service are disastrous.

- Foreign financial companies are lining up to offer their services in Norway. Eirik Bunaes at the Norwegian Securities Board says the development will result in harder competition for Norwegian financial companies.

- Swedish power company Vattenfall wants to build cooperation with 20 energy distribution companies in Norway. Leif Gromstad, Vattenfall's Norwegian managing director, says the company will buy and enter colloboration agreements with the Norwegian firms.
